title: Strata — AI-First, Git-Compatible Source Control
excerpt: Git-compatible, AI-first source control for developers and coding agents. Coordinate concurrent changes, preserve context, and integrate code safely.
content_html:
Source control for humans and coding agents

Multiple agents. One codebase. No lost work.1

Strata gives AI coding agents isolated workspaces, persistent development context, and safe concurrent integration, while keeping your existing Git workflows.

Keep your Git tools. Give your agents something better to work with.

01 — The problem

Git wasn't designed for a hundred agents working at once.

Git is excellent distributed version control, and it already supports concurrent, distributed development. The friction sits in the workflow layered on top: branches, rebases, pull requests and merge queues were designed around a handful of people who remember what they did yesterday.

When many autonomous agents modify the same codebase, that workflow turns into orchestration work. Someone, or some script, has to create branches, sequence merges, retry rebases and carry knowledge from one session to the next. Strata moves coordination, integration and context into the source control system itself.

  1. 01Branch proliferationOne branch per task per agent, each to be named, tracked and cleaned up.
  2. 02Repeated rebasingEvery merge to main moves the base under every other open branch.
  3. 03Merge orchestrationSomeone has to decide the order in which work lands.
  4. 04Coordination overheadAgents cannot see who else is changing the same files.
  5. 05Concurrent conflictsText conflict markers are written for people, not programs.
  6. 06Lost session contextWhat an agent learned ends with its session.
  7. 07Fragmented knowledgeDecisions live in chat logs, PR comments and prompts.
  8. 08Fragile automationScripts around Git break on the edge cases agents hit constantly.

02 — How Strata works

From isolated work to integrated history.

  1. 01An agent receives a taskTracked with an owner, dependencies and status.

  2. 02Strata creates a workspaceIsolated, at the current authoritative revision.

  3. 03Context is retrievedDecisions, discoveries and checkpoints for the task.

  4. 04The agent submits changesAs a candidate, not a push to a branch.

  5. 05Strata validates and integratesAgainst current state. Overlaps return as structured conflicts.

  6. 06History and context persistWith provenance, for the next agent or developer.

03 — Core capabilities

Source control primitives for agents.

✓ EVALUATED marks areas covered by the reported private evaluation.

01

Isolated agent workspaces

Agents work independently without requiring conventional branch management for every task.

02✓ EVALUATED

Transactional integration

Changes are integrated against authoritative repository state using concurrency-safe publication mechanisms.

03

Persistent development context

Task intent, decisions, discoveries, provenance, and handoffs survive individual sessions.

04✓ EVALUATED

Structured conflict resolution

Conflicts become actionable data that coding agents can inspect and resolve.

05

Multi-agent coordination

Tasks, dependencies, agent identities, and progress can be managed across concurrent development activity.

06✓ EVALUATED

Git compatibility

Existing Git clients and workflows remain available over Git HTTP and SSH.

07✓ EVALUATED

MCP and native APIs

Agents interact with Strata through purpose-built interfaces over MCP and gRPC.

08✓ EVALUATED

Identity and access control

Human users and agents have distinct identities, permissions, and delegated authority.

09✓ EVALUATED

Self-hosting

Run Strata on your own infrastructure, with backups and recovery.

04 — Git compatibility

Keep Git. Change the workflow.

Developers keep cloning, fetching and pushing with the Git clients they already use, over HTTP or SSH. Agents work through Strata's native interfaces: they get a workspace, submit candidates, receive structured conflicts and read and write context. Both paths read and write the same authoritative repository state.

Compatibility is scoped to the operations covered by tests. The Git compatibility reference lists supported operations and known limitations.

05 — Multi-agent development

Three agents, one repository.

Two changes integrate cleanly. The third overlaps and comes back as a structured conflict instead of being merged silently. Integration safety means acknowledged changes are not lost; it does not make the combined code semantically correct. Your tests and review still do that.

Keyboard: focus the figure, ← → to step, R to reset.

06 — Persistent context

Your agents forget. Your repository shouldn't.

Agents record what they learn as structured context: task objectives, architectural decisions, implementation discoveries, progress checkpoints and handoffs. Each record carries its source revision and a status, so it can be verified or superseded as the code moves on.

Strata stores what agents explicitly write. It does not read a model's private reasoning. Context is evidence, and the next agent checks it against the current repository state.

07 — Concurrency evidence

Built for concurrent development. Tested with 100 agents.

Distinct agents submitting concurrently
100

Acknowledged changes
100

Acknowledged changes lost
01

Agents in the integration and conflict-resolution test
3

1 — Controlled evaluation on a single private deployment backed by PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage. The results describe behaviour under those test conditions. They are not a scalability limit, a throughput benchmark or a production reliability guarantee.

08 — Architecture

Infrastructure, not another coding assistant.

Strata is not an LLM and does not write code. It is the system of record that coding agents and developers work against. The backend is written in Go and ships as Docker containers, with PostgreSQL for metadata and S3-compatible object storage for repository content.

It does not depend on a particular model provider. Any agent that speaks MCP, the native API or Git can use it.

09 — Self-hosting

Your code. Your infrastructure. Your control.

Strata is open source and runs on infrastructure you operate. Repository content, context records and identities stay inside your network. The installation guide covers prerequisites, configuration, backups and recovery.

Deployment model
runtimeGo services in Docker
metadataPostgreSQL
objectsS3-compatible storage (evaluated on Ceph)
accessGit HTTP / SSH, MCP, gRPC
statusEVALUATION · NOT YET PRODUCTION-READY

The current deployment has passed evaluation of PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage, Git HTTP and SSH, IAM, MCP and gRPC, recovery and backups. Strata has not been declared production-ready; the roadmap lists what remains.

Your agents should collaborate, not compete for the same branch.

Give coding agents a shared development foundation built for concurrency, context, and safe integration.
